L1.run_record: FAST: Completed. SLOW: waits (read only, re-check every 2 min up to 25 min); once FAST's record is Completed it proceeds and records No-op for this scope; if FAST were still Started at 10:33, SLOW ends 'Partial: lease held by FAST <run id>' with no row written
L1.answer: FAST holds the lease. Both records say Started 10:08, and both prompts say 'if both are Started, the earlier start holds it, and in the same minute FAST does.' SLOW only reads, re-checking every 2 minutes for up to 25 minutes. FAST sends the Sponsored yes next steps reply and ends Completed. SLOW then proceeds, finds nothing due on the row and ends No-op, or Partial 'lease held by FAST' if FAST were still Started at 10:33.
L1.findings: 1/ Residual race. The rule is write-own-record-then-read-the-other with a fixed tie-break, and no run re-reads after deciding. Suppose SLOW writes and reads before FAST's record exists, in the same minute. SLOW then proceeds, and FAST, reading later, sees a same-minute SLOW record and also proceeds by the tie-break. Both write rows. The as-stated same-second case (both writes before both reads) is safe. Fix: the tie-break should only let FAST proceed if SLOW's record shows it has not yet passed its lease check, or both runs should re-read after a short delay. 2/ 'Earlier start' is compared by the record's Date/minute. The Summary carries HH:MM only, so the tie-break covers up to 59 seconds of real difference.
L1.notes: FAST LEASE and SLOW LEASE lines are symmetric with the same tie-break; SLOW's wait is 'up to 25 minutes', FAST's 'up to 10 minutes'.

L2.run_record: Case 1: 'Run zoya FAST 2026-10-27 11:38 JST: Partial' with 'lease held by SLOW <run id>', no row written. Case 2: Completed.
L2.answer: Case 1 (SLOW Started 10:50, 48 minutes old): the lease counts as held, because a Started record 'begun under 60 minutes ago' holds it. FAST only reads and re-checks every 2 minutes for up to 10 minutes (11:38 to 11:48). At 11:48 the record is 58 minutes old, so still held. FAST ends Partial 'lease held by SLOW <run id>' with no row written, and the reply goes at the 12:38 FAST run, when the lease is stale. Case 2 (Started 10:30, 68 minutes old): stale, so FAST proceeds at once and sends the reply. The exact limits: stale at 60 minutes (a lease is held only while 'begun under 60 minutes ago'); FAST waits up to 10 minutes, re-checking every 2 (Bash sleep 120); SLOW waits up to 25.
L2.findings: 1/ Nothing ever marks a crashed run's record Failed; it stays Started forever and only ages out at 60 minutes. Harmless to the lease, but run reports and the good-morning check will show a perpetual Started. 2/ In Case 1 the crash delays a sponsored-yes reply by a full hour (09:55 inbound answered 12:38), because FAST's 10-minute wait ends 2 minutes before the lease goes stale at 11:50. A re-check at expiry, or a wait that runs until the lease would go stale when that falls within a few minutes, would answer at 11:50. 3/ SLOW's RECONCILE would flag the reply as stuck only after 2 hours (11:55), and only on a SLOW run (next 16:50).
L2.notes: FAST: 'Before your first row write, read the latest run record with Source ID starting "run:zoya:slow:": one still at Started, begun under 60 minutes ago, holds the lease ... re-checking every 2 minutes (Bash sleep 120, else between read steps) for up to 10 minutes; still held, end Partial "lease held by SLOW <run id>" with no row written.'
